is_anopheles.evidence: All tests were carried out using 2-5-day-old non-blood-fed female mosquitoes of the insecticide-susceptible Kisumu strain of Anopheles gambiae s.s. reared in the Liverpool Insect Testing Establishment (LITE) insectaries at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine (LSTM) (page 4).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study is a laboratory bioassay evaluation of repurposed agricultural and veterinary insecticides on the susceptible Kisumu laboratory colony; no genetic markers or molecular assays were performed.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotyping was performed, and no genotype or allele counts/frequencies are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: All mosquitoes tested were from the laboratory-maintained Kisumu colony of Anopheles gambiae s.s. reared at LSTM (page 4). No field-collected mosquitoes or progeny thereof were tested.

is_primary_study.evidence: The paper presents primary experimental laboratory bioassay screening data for 40 chemical compounds.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No field mosquito collection dates exist.

assessment.summary: This study evaluates a screening cascade of 40 repurposed agrochemical and animal health insecticides using topical application, tarsal contact, and modified CDC bottle bioassays against the laboratory-reared insecticide-susceptible Kisumu strain of Anopheles gambiae s.s. No field mosquitoes were tested and no resistance marker genotyping was performed.
exclusion_reasons: Does not report any target resistance markers
Does not report extractable genotype data
Does not test an African field population (only laboratory colony Kisumu strain)
